style: An Italian High Renaissance oil painting of Caesar's wars in Gaul, 58 BC, in the manner of Andrea Mantegna's Triumphs of Caesar, Raphael and Titian: classical Greco-Roman grandeur, figures modelled like antique marble sculpture, noble classical drapery and gesture, a monumental balanced composition with a deep perspective, armour, standards and architecture taken from Roman antiquity, rich glowing Venetian colour — ultramarine, vermilion, gold, warm flesh — under a luminous sky, smooth polished glazes in the manner of the old masters, crisp drawing, heroic but grave. Roman legionaries in mail shirts, bronze Montefortino helmets and curved oval shields; Gauls with long hair, moustaches, checked trousers, cloaks and torcs. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: Julius Caesar riding at full gallop along a Roman road in southern Gaul with a small escort of cavalry in red cloaks, dust rising, cypresses and vineyards beside the road, hard bright sun.Roman legionaries wear mail shirts, bronze Montefortino helmets and curved oval shields; Gauls have long hair, moustaches, checked trousers, cloaks and torcs.
